## Cheat sheet (90 seconds)

| Task | Tool | Call |
|---|---|---|
| translate / rev-comp | Biopython | `Seq(s).translate()`, `Seq(s).reverse_complement()` |
| parse FASTA/FASTQ | Biopython | `SeqIO.parse(handle, "fasta")` |
| per-base quality | Biopython | `rec.letter_annotations["phred_quality"]` |
| k-mers | (yours, P3) | `Counter(seq[i:i+k] for i in ...)` |
| read/write BAM | pysam | `AlignmentFile("f.bam", "wb", header=...)` |
| fetch by region | pysam | `bam.fetch("chr1", start, end)` (needs `.bai` index) |
| genomic intervals | GenomicRanges (R, local) | `GRanges(seqnames, IRanges(start, end), strand)` |

::: {.callout-note}
## Why this day is special
Everything runs **live in your browser** — Biopython and pysam are compiled
for WebAssembly. No server, no install. The only thing that *can't* run
in-browser is R's Bioconductor (Day 5 covers the workaround for that).
:::

## Biopython: the sequence object

```{pyodide}
#| label: seq-basics
from Bio.Seq import Seq

dna = Seq("ATGGCCATTGTAATGGGCCGCTGAAAGGGTGCCCGATAG")

print(f"length:      {len(dna)}")
print(f"rev-comp:    {dna.reverse_complement()}")
print(f"translation: {dna.translate()}")       # note the internal stop!
print(f"GC:          {sum(b in 'GC' for b in dna) / len(dna) * 100:.2f}%")
```

Look closely at the translation: `MAIVMGR*KGAR*` — there's an **internal
stop codon** (`TGA` at position 21) before the terminal `TAG`. A naive
ORF-finder that assumes "first ATG → last stop" gets this wrong. We won't.

## FASTA in, records out

```{pyodide}
#| label: fasta
import io
from Bio import SeqIO

fasta = """>ENST1 some transcript
ATGGCCATTGTAATGGGCCGCTGAAAGGGTGCCCGATAG
>ENST2 short one
ATGGCCATTGTAATGGGCCGCTGAAAGGGTGCCCGATAGAAA
"""

for rec in SeqIO.parse(io.StringIO(fasta), "fasta"):
    gc = sum(b in "GC" for b in rec.seq) / len(rec.seq) * 100
    print(f"{rec.id:8s} {len(rec.seq):3d} nt   GC {gc:.1f}%   ({rec.description})")
```

`rec.id` = first whitespace token; `rec.description` = the whole header.
In real pipelines `SeqIO.parse("transcripts.fa", "fasta")` streams a file
the same way — this shape (lazy iterator of records) scales to gigabases.

## An honest ORF scanner (3 frames)

```{pyodide}
#| label: orfs
def orfs(seq: str, min_nt: int = 15) -> list[tuple[int, int, int]]:
    """(frame, start, end) of ATG->stop open reading frames, 1-based frame."""
    stops = {"TAA", "TAG", "TGA"}
    out = []
    for frame in range(3):
        i = frame
        while i < len(seq) - 2:
            if seq[i:i+3] == "ATG":
                j = i
                while j < len(seq) - 2:
                    if seq[j:j+3] in stops:
                        if j + 3 - i >= min_nt:
                            out.append((frame + 1, i, j + 3))
                        break
                    j += 3
            i += 3 if seq[i:i+3] == "ATG" else 1
    return out

dna = "ATGGCCATTGTAATGGGCCGCTGAAAGGGTGCCCGATAG"
print("ORFs (frame, start, end):", orfs(dna))
```

One ORF, `(frame 1, 0, 24)` — the internal `TGA` cuts it short, exactly as
the translation showed. The scanner breaks at the *first* stop after each
ATG and moves on; it does not scan through stops (that's what real gene
finders with dynamic programming are for — Week 5's HMMs are the conceptual
cousin).

## FASTQ: bases + quality, the QC currency

```{pyodide}
#| label: fastq
import io
import numpy as np
from Bio import SeqIO

fastq = """@read1 good one
ATGGCC
+
IIIIII
@read2 has a bad tail
GGCCTT
+
#####!
"""
recs = list(SeqIO.parse(io.StringIO(fastq), "fastq"))

for rec in recs:
    q = np.array(rec.letter_annotations["phred_quality"])
    print(f"{rec.id:20s} meanQ {q.mean():5.1f}   minQ {q.min():2d}")

# the classic filter: drop reads whose mean Q < 20 (1% error rate)
good = [r for r in recs
        if np.mean(r.letter_annotations["phred_quality"]) >= 20]
print(f"kept {len(good)} / {len(recs)} reads")
```

Phred Q = −10·log₁₀(P(error)). Q20 = 1% error, Q30 = 0.1%, Q40 = 0.01%.
The `'I'` character encodes Q40 (`#` is Q2, `!` is Q0) under Illumina 1.8+
encoding — if your FASTQ predates 1.8, the same characters mean different
Q values, and QC thresholds silently shift. When in doubt: `head` a file,
check which Q range the qualities span.

## pysam: your first BAM, written and read in the browser

```{pyodide}
#| label: pysam
import pysam

sam_text = ("@HD\tVN:1.6\tSO:coordinate\n"
            "@SQ\tSN:chr1\tLN:1000\n"
            "r1\t0\tchr1\t100\t60\t4M\t*\t0\t0\tATGC\tIIII\n"
            "r2\t0\tchr1\t300\t60\t4M\t*\t0\t0\tGGCC\tIIII\n"
            "r3\t16\tchr1\t500\t60\t4M\t*\t0\t0\tTTAA\tIIII\n")

# SAM -> BAM (the lesson's VFS is writable!)
with open("reads.sam", "w") as f:
    f.write(sam_text)
with pysam.AlignmentFile("reads.sam", "r") as fin, \
     pysam.AlignmentFile("reads.bam", "wb", header=fin.header) as fout:
    for read in fin:
        fout.write(read)

with pysam.AlignmentFile("reads.bam", "rb") as bam:
    for r in bam:
        print(f"{r.query_name}  pos={r.reference_start + 1}  "
              f"reverse={r.is_reverse}  mapQ={r.mapping_quality}")
```

The SAM flags decode into properties: `16` = reverse-strand alignment
(`is_reverse`), 4 = unmapped (`is_unmapped`), 2 = proper pair. Now index it
and **fetch by region** — the operation that makes BAM essential (random
access to a 100 GB file in milliseconds):

```{pyodide}
#| label: pysam-fetch
import pysam

pysam.index("reads.bam")                       # writes reads.bam.bai
with pysam.AlignmentFile("reads.bam", "rb") as bam:
    region = list(bam.fetch("chr1", 99, 200))  # 0-based half-open!
    print("chr1:100-200 ->", [r.query_name for r in region])
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Coordinate systems (source of ~all region-fetch bugs)
BAM internals and pysam `fetch()` are **0-based, half-open** `[start, end)`.
SAM text, most genomes browsers, and human conversation are **1-based,
inclusive**. `r1` sits at SAM position 100 = pysam `reference_start` 99;
fetching `chr1:100-200` in pysam is `(99, 200)`. Write it on a sticky note.
:::

## The GenomicRanges mental model (R, conceptual + local)

Ranges libraries (GenomicRanges/IRanges, pyranges in Python) store
**intervals, not sequences**: `(chrom, start, end, strand)` with *vectorized*
algebra — `findOverlaps()`, `reduce()`, `width()`, `coverage()`. The mindset
shift from positions-to-loops is "one vector of ranges, one verb" — Pattern 1
again, for coordinates. There's a runnable local script in
`scripts/granges_demo.R` for after class (Bioconductor doesn't compile to
WebAssembly — the one thing this day can't do live).

## Drills (live pad)

```{pyodide}
#| label: drills
from Bio.Seq import Seq

# 1. Translate "ATGGCC" and "CCAGGC" — same protein? which frame(s)?

# 2. rev-comp of a palindrome: "GAATTC" — predict before running

# 3. GC of "ACGT" repeated 10 times — exact value, then code it

# 4. Count 4-mers of the Day 3 transcript — how many distinct? (n-k+1 total)

# 5. orfs("ATGGGCTAA", min_nt=9) — predict, then run

# 6. In pysam terms: SAM position 1,000,000 is reference_start = ?
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Expected answers
1. Both → "MA" — same reading frame, different window; translation starts
   at the sequence's own frame, there's no magic
2. "GAATTC" — palindromic (EcoRI site!): rev-comp equals itself
3. 50.0 — ACGT has 2 of 4 GC; repetition doesn't change composition
4. 39 − 4 + 1 = 36 windows; distinct depends on sequence (here 30)
5. `[(1, 0, 9)]` — ATG→TAA is 9 nt, passes min_nt=9
6. `999_999` — 1-based SAM − 1 = 0-based start
:::

## Exercises

### Exercise 1 — a Tm calculator class

Minimum-GC oligonucleotide Tm estimate: `2°C × (A+T) + 4°C × (G+C)`.
Wrap it as a class with a `tm` property (W3D1 style).

```{pyodide}
#| exercise: ex-w4d3-tm
class Oligo:
    def __init__(self, seq: str):
        self.seq = seq.upper()

    @property
    def tm(self) -> float:
        ______

o = Oligo("ACGTACGT")
print(o.tm)     # 2*4 + 4*4 = 24
```

::: {.hint exercise="ex-w4d3-tm"}
`return 2 * sum(b in "AT" for b in self.seq) + 4 * sum(b in "GC" for b in self.seq)`
:::

::: {.solution exercise="ex-w4d3-tm"}
```python
class Oligo:
    def __init__(self, seq: str):
        self.seq = seq.upper()

    @property
    def tm(self) -> float:
        at = sum(b in "AT" for b in self.seq)
        gc = sum(b in "GC" for b in self.seq)
        return 2 * at + 4 * gc
```
:::

### Exercise 2 — the FASTQ QC pass

Filter reads: keep if mean Q ≥ 25 AND length ≥ 6. Report kept/total and the
mean length of kept reads.

```{pyodide}
#| exercise: ex-w4d3-qc
import io
import numpy as np
from Bio import SeqIO

fastq = ("@r1\nATGGCCATT\n+\nIIIIIIIII\n"
         "@r2\nGGCCTTAA\n+\nIIIII###\n"
         "@r3\nGC\n+\nII\n")
recs = list(SeqIO.parse(io.StringIO(fastq), "fastq"))

kept = ______

print(f"kept {len(kept)} / {len(recs)}")
```

::: {.hint exercise="ex-w4d3-qc"}
Two conditions on `letter_annotations["phred_quality"]` and
`len(rec.seq)`; r1 passes, r2 fails mean-Q, r3 fails length.
:::

::: {.solution exercise="ex-w4d3-qc"}
```python
kept = [r for r in recs
        if np.mean(r.letter_annotations["phred_quality"]) >= 25
        and len(r.seq) >= 6]
# kept = [r1] — r2's ### tail drags mean Q below 25, r3 is too short
```
:::

### Exercise 3 — codon usage table

Count codon frequencies across all 3 frames of the Day 3 transcript —
which codon appears most? (This is a real metric: codon usage bias.)

```{pyodide}
#| exercise: ex-w4d3-codons
from collections import Counter

seq = "ATGGCCATTGTAATGGGCCGCTGAAAGGGTGCCCGATAG"
codons = Counter(
    ______
)
print(codons.most_common(3))
```

::: {.hint exercise="ex-w4d3-codons"}
One frame: `seq[i:i+3] for i in range(0, len(seq) - 2, 3)`. All frames:
loop start offset 0/1/2.
:::

::: {.solution exercise="ex-w4d3-codons"}
```python
codons = Counter(
    seq[i:i+3]
    for off in range(3)
    for i in range(off, len(seq) - 2, 3)
)
# [('GCC', 3), ('ATG', 2), ('GGG', 2)] — GCC (Ala) wins
```
:::

Using the lesson's `reads.bam`: count how many reads map to each strand,
and list the names of reverse-strand reads.

```{pyodide}

import pysam

with pysam.AlignmentFile("reads.bam", "rb") as bam:

```

::: {.hint exercise="ex-w4d3-bam"}
Iterate reads; `r.is_reverse`; collect names into a list when True.
:::

::: {.solution exercise="ex-w4d3-bam"}
```python
with pysam.AlignmentFile("reads.bam", "rb") as bam:
    reads = list(bam)
    fwd = [r.query_name for r in reads if not r.is_reverse]
    rev = [r.query_name for r in reads if r.is_reverse]
    print(f"+ {len(fwd)}: {fwd}   - {len(rev)}: {rev}")
# + 2: ['r1', 'r2']   - 1: ['r3']
```
:::

### Exercise 5 — k-mer signature distance (ties the week together)

Two sequences, k-mer profiles (P3's `kmer_counts`), Euclidean distance on
shared-kmer counts. This is a miniature sequence-signature classifier —
the idea sourmash scales up.

```{pyodide}
#| exercise: ex-w4d3-kmerdist
from collections import Counter
import numpy as np

def profile(seq: str, k: int = 2) -> dict[str, int]:
    return dict(Counter(seq[i:i+k] for i in range(len(seq) - k + 1)))

def kmer_distance(a: str, b: str, k: int = 2) -> float:
    ______

print(kmer_distance("ATGGCC", "ATGGCC"))   # 0.0
print(kmer_distance("ATGGCC", "TTACGG"))
```

::: {.hint exercise="ex-w4d3-kmerdist"}
Build both profiles; take the union of keys; sum `(a.get(k,0) - b.get(k,0))**2`;
return `sqrt`.
:::

::: {.solution exercise="ex-w4d3-kmerdist"}
```python
def kmer_distance(a, b, k=2):
    pa, pb = profile(a, k), profile(b, k)
    keys = set(pa) | set(pb)
    return float(np.sqrt(sum((pa.get(kmer, 0) - pb.get(kmer, 0))**2
                             for kmer in keys)))
```
:::

## Common pitfalls (real ones)

::: {.callout-warning}
## 1. 0-based vs 1-based coordinates
`fetch()` half-open 0-based; SAM/ground conversation 1-based inclusive.
Every pipeline has this bug once — the sticky note is cheaper.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## 2. Phred encodings pre-Illumina-1.8
Same characters, different Q values (Phred+64). If QC thresholds behave
weirdly on old data, check the encoding before the library.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## 3. Translation stops at the first stop (by default)
Biopython's `.translate()` returns `*` inside the protein but toffee-nosed
tools differ: some cut at the first stop, some (with `cds=True`) require
no internal stops. Know which contract your downstream tool expects.
:::

## Self-quiz — predict the output

```{pyodide}
#| label: quiz
# Q1: len of the rev-comp of a 39-nt sequence?
# Q2: Seq("atgc").translate() — does case matter? (run it!)
# Q3: Q30 = what error rate?
# Q4: pysam: fetch("chr1", 0, 100) covers SAM positions ...?
# Q5: k-mers: 200-nt read, k=31 — how many windows?
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Quiz answers
1. 39 — rev-comp preserves length (complement then reverse)
2. It errors or returns empty-translation for lowercase — Biopython expects
   uppercase; always `.upper()` input sequences (you saw `.upper()` in
   every production snippet)
3. 0.1% (Q = −10·log10 p)
4. SAM 1–100 (0-based half-open shifted up by one)
5. 200 − 31 + 1 = 170
:::
